government.note: Government type as on 1 January 2000: under the 1995 constitution the directly elected President held executive power; the office of Prime Minister had been abolished and a State Minister coordinated the government (recorded here in the Prime Minister office, as in the Wikipedia list). The February 2004 constitutional amendment re-established the office of Prime Minister, appointed by the President, who kept most executive powers under Saakashvili. Amendments passed between 2012 and 2018 transferred executive power to the Prime Minister, who is accountable to Parliament, and made the presidency largely ceremonial (per the Wikipedia article on the Prime Minister of Georgia). Since 2024 the President is elected by an Electoral Assembly. The type and power weights are kept as in 2000; from the 2012-2018 reforms the system is parliamentary.

system.note: In 1999: 150 seats by national party-list PR and the rest in single-member constituencies, plus 12 deputies elected in 1992 for Abkhazia, who kept their seats because no election was held there. The 2003 referendum cut Parliament to 150 seats from 2008; the 2024 election was fully proportional. The threshold was not checked. seats_2000 is the result of the October-November 1999 election.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the October 1999 party-list vote (shares of all valid list votes): Union of Citizens of Georgia 44.48% (big tent, as Wikipedia describes it), Revival bloc 26.82% (Adjaran regionalism), Industry Will Save Georgia 7.54% (economic nationalism, recorded as national conservative), Georgian Labour Party 7.02% (left populist), communist lists 1.78% (Unified Communists, Communists-Stalinists, Revived Communists), and all other lists 12.36% (big tent).

claims.note: Georgia regards Abkhazia as part of its territory; the 1999 Parliament kept 12 deputies elected for Abkhazia in 1992 because no election could be held there.
Georgia regards South Ossetia as part of its territory.
